notes: No document collected. The college-level source is the Provost-appointed working group's 'Informational Guide: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Lafayette Faculty and Staff Members' (about 41 pages, with sample course policies), linked from https://provost.lafayette.edu/policies-and-procedures and https://citls.lafayette.edu/2023/08/23/guidance-on-generative-ai/. It is a Google Doc (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1p1PNSIfc6mLQ5q2gt__InVsM6Wl18-TmD125cHZsL2k/edit) that requires a Google sign-in, so fetch_text.py (edit and export routes) got only the login page. The CITLS page 'Teaching and Generative AI: Curated Resources' (citls.lafayette.edu/?p=18373) is a resource list with no rules, and the provost page only links to the guide, so neither was collected. Search snippets say faculty voted that syllabi must include course-specific AI policies, but no official text was retrieved. No CS department AI policy was found; the Biology department's academic integrity statement mentions generative AI but is not a computing unit. The only known URL (CS150 syllabus, Wayback) is a course document and is deferred.
